cars.variant: D8-120 Figoni & Falaschi cabriolet — 1939 Toyota museum reference
cars.specification_market: Historic Delage D8 production-road family, selected 1939 D8-120 Figoni and Falaschi cabriolet at Toyota Automobile Museum, public automobile entry 333. Eleven attributes map to the exact museum record, with units verified in its linked technical-table rendering script. Keep quoted 4750 cm3, 86 kW/115 HP at 3800 min-1 and 1805-kg vehicle mass without an inferred power test standard, dry/kerb definition or extra displacement precision. The earlier D8 Super Sports 4-litre/100-mph account and different 1937 Aerosport data are not transferred. No gearbox, torque, brakes, suspension, seating count, measured speed or acceleration inferred. The museum calls the selected body a cabriolet; the photo filename Phaeton is retained only as supplied attribution title. Group historic D8, D8S and D8-100/120 road derivatives once conservatively; no individual body, engine, chassis or year adds another record. Dedicated GP/record cars and replicas are not admitted.
cars.summary: The Delage D8 is an established French straight-eight sporting-road family, including the Super Sports and later high-performance D8-120. It represents an important pre-war grand-touring tradition rather than rarity or luxury alone. Count the historic D8 road family once across engines, bodies and years; individual coachwork, competition machines and replicas do not create extra records.

sources.notes: Page shell and linked public data source https://toyota-automobile-museum.jp/archives/data.json read, selecting only automobile entry id 333, code 01. Complete relevant selected record read in English and Japanese. The linked /en/archives/detail.js was inspected for id routing and technical-table units: dimensions/wheelbase mm, vehicle mass kg, displacement cm3 and output min-1. All eleven attributes use this exact reference. Output remains quoted 86 kW/115 HP at 3800 min-1 without an inferred power test standard; vehicle mass has no assumed dry/kerb basis. No measured top speed, acceleration, transmission, suspension or brake specification inferred. Generic marque GP history and the sexist luxury-car epithet are not imported. No claim of visually inspecting a rendered museum browser table.

sources.title: Home — D8 and D8 Super Sports road-car history
sources.notes: Full relevant historical account read. Distinguishes production road models from dedicated racing programmes and describes the D8 straight-eight family and sporting Super Sports version. Its 4-litre and 100-mph statements are not specifications for the selected later D8-120; no speed field imported. Club-wide race victories, 15 S 8 GP results, generic prototype endurance-test mileage and unqualified superiority claims do not become D8 road-car achievements.
